channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
item.description: The chipmaking giant says it is looking into reports by The New York Times that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

item.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
item.description: NASA needs more recruits in order to return to the moon after being gone more than half a century.

item.title: Arrest made in deadly shooting during Winston-Salem State homecoming weekend
item.description: It is too early to tell whether the shootings were connected, police say.

item.title: NVIDIA announces investigation of CEO amid foreign intelligence target allegations
item.description: Jensen Huang "is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA," the company said.

item.title: Nvidia to probe reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.

item.title: Ron DeSantis hasn't made final decision on 2028 run: Sources
item.description: In the days leading up to and after the midterms, DeSantis has ramped up his media appearances, reflecting on what went wrong for the Republican Party.

item.title: Pope Leo criticises Milei’s austerity in Argentina, says growth must benefit all
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his tour began, facing calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei. The visit to Buenos Aires is the first by a pontiff to the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades.

item.title: Pope Leo in Latin America: Papal Politics and Peru
item.description: Pope Leo heads to Argentina for the second leg of his South America tour, where he's expected to draw the biggest turnout of his Papacy so far. The pontiff has wrapped up his first visit to Uruguay. Colleen Dulle, Vatican Correspondent at America Magazine and the co-host of the 'Inside the Vatican' podcast, joins us to analyse the significance of his Latin American tour.

item.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot begins the hard work of forging a coalition government
item.description: Israel's ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot was tapped by President Isaac Herzog to try to form a government Sunday evening. But his lack of a clear majority in parliament will make trying to forge a coalition alongside the country's divided minor parties an uphill struggle.

item.title: Nvidia launches 'foreign intelligence' investigation after CEO admits affair
item.description: Tech giant Nvidia says it is investigating reports that chief executive Jensen ⁠Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

item.title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities say
item.description: A boat carrying migrants along the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off the coast of Senegal, killed at least 34 people, authorities said Sunday. Only one survivor has so far been found, and "an indeterminate number" are still missing.

item.title: Government considering banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
item.description: The government is seriously considering banning children from online sales platforms such as eBay and Vinted, the culture secretary has said.

item.title: El-Sayed: Democrats will work with Trump if 'he wants to act serious'
item.description: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed joins "This Week" after his historic victory against Republican Mike Rogers in the midterm election.

item.title: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms: 'It's safe to say that we are a blue state'
item.description: Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms joins "This Week" to discuss Democrats' sweeping victories, and her historic win in formerly red Georgia.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands without power
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday following Russian airstrikes targeting the country's energy infrastructure. Moscow has intensified its attacks as winter approaches, leaving residents in Kyiv and other parts of the country struggling with power cuts as temperatures continue to drop. Clemence Waller reports.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot receives mandate to form government
item.description: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has officially been tasked with forming the country's next government, following a formal announcement by President Isaac Herzog. He now has up to six weeks to negotiate with potential coalition partners and secure a parliamentary majority. While an alliance with Arab Israeli parties appears to be the easiest option mathematically, it remains politically sensitive. Eisenkot must now navigate difficult negotiations to build a coalition capable of replacing Benjamin Netanyahu. Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

item.title: Spain's Alcaraz beats error-prone Shelton to win Paris Masters for first time
item.description: Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to American player Ben Shelton in the US Open in September as he inched ahead of his rival Sunday to win the Paris Masters for the first time. It was Shelton's first defeat in a Masters final.

item.title: Pete Hegseth could soon face impeachment proceedings
item.description: Pete Hegseth could soon face impeachment proceedings as Democrats plan what to do with their majorities in both houses of Congress.

item.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
item.description: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.

item.title: The week in pictures: US midterms 'Blue Wave', French protests and Dakar Youth Olympics
item.description: From the Democratic Party's big wins in the US midterm elections to France's ongoing student-led protests and the first Olympic sports event held on African soil, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.

item.title: Election 2026 live updates: Trump says US took 'giant step back' through midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump continued to criticize the results of Tuesday's midterm elections.

item.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
item.description: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

item.title: Seven dead and 114 injured in train crash near Cairo
item.description: At least seven people have died and more than 100 have been left injured in a major train crash south of Cairo, according to the Egyptian Chief Prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Schools to stop teaching GCSEs early in curriculum overhaul
item.description: Secondary schools will be told to stop teaching GCSEs to students until they reach Year 10 in a bid to keep younger children engaged, according to the government.

item.title: US voters reject AI data centres: could the backlash spread to France?
item.description: In Tuesday’s US midterm elections, voters weighed in on more than 40 local measures on data centres, and sided against them in all but one. With Democrats taking control of Congress in January and new governors in Texas and Georgia calling for moratoriums, the AI building boom faces its toughest political test yet.

item.title: Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsens
item.description: One month into the Yemeni government's offensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, fighting continues to escalate along the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the humanitarian crisis is worsening, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced and the country facing the threat of catastrophe. Rula Amin, Senior Communications Advisor and spokesperson at UNHCR at Amman, in Jordan, shares further details.

item.title: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting
item.description: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.

item.title: French skipper wins Route du Rhum
item.description: French sailor Tom Laperche has won the Route du Rhum, setting a new record in the transatlantic yacht race. The 29-year-old crossed the finish line in Guadeloupe on his first attempt, beating the previous 2022 record by around six hours. A remarkable debut in one of sailing's toughest competitions!

item.title: Mourning in Poland after mass shooting
item.description: Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 16 injured. The 24-year-old Polish suspect was reportedly fascinated by far-right ideologies. Authorities are investigating the possible extremist motive as Krakow's main square remains sealed. Two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.

item.title: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French FM says
item.description: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.

item.title: Pope Leo urges men to respect wives amid Latin American femicide crisis
item.description: Pope Leo XIV urged men to respect their wives as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America. The region recorded nearly 20,000 instances of women being killed over the past five years alone, most of them murdered by a current or former partner.

item.title: Weather warning issued for parts of UK amid 'perfect recipe' for fog
item.description: Weather conditions in the UK are creating the "perfect recipe" for fog, the Met Office has said, as it issued a warning over travel conditions.

item.title: 'Human rights and freedom have ceased': Newspaper that defied Kremlin pays price
One dead in Russia after Ukraine drone attack - as emergency workers struck by Moscow
item.description: One person has died after being hit by a Ukrainian drone attack in western Russia, while Moscow has struck emergency workers on rescue missions.

item.title: ‘10 times more painful’: Menstrual disorders fuel calls to ban tear gas at French protests
item.description: French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests that have roiled France in recent weeks, sometimes causing grievous injuries. Thousands of accounts of women experiencing acutely painful periods and increased bleeding are further challenging assumptions that the chemical irritant carries only minor consequences.

item.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
item.description: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.

item.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
item.description: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.

item.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
item.description: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.

item.title: 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games: Golden Double for Senegal
item.description: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.

item.title: Diwali: Over one billion people mark victory of light over darkness
item.description: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the deity celebrated during the festival, festivities included performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.

item.title: Paraguay: Senate impeached Peña rather than accept his offer to resign
item.description: Paraguay's ousted president, Santiago Peña, has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Initially placed under house arrest, he has since been transferred to a military facility for his own safety. Nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts after regulators seized control of the online bank. Repayments are now under way, but protests continue as customers demand access to their money. Peña denies any wrongdoing. Jack Pownall reports.

item.title: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 27 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Donald Trump wants UFC fighters as assistants
item.description: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.

item.title: Israel's Arab-led parties gain influence
item.description: Arab-led parties have endorsed Gadi Eisenkot despite his ruling out a coalition with them. Their support is driven by a shared goal: removing Benjamin Netanyahu from power. But could these parties ultimately hold the balance of power in forming Israel's next government? Antonia Kerrigan reports.

item.title: Trump 'only kidding' about offering UFC boss press secretary job
item.description: Donald Trump has said he was "only kidding" about UFC boss Dana White becoming White House press secretary.

item.title: Trump says chief of staff Susie Wiles out, Stephen Miller will replace her
item.description: Trump said his top aide Stephen Miller will replace her in the job.

item.title: Briton among six killed by 'far-right' gunman in Krakow rampage
item.description: A 32-year-old British man is among six people killed in a mass shooting in Krakow, in which another Briton was wounded, Polish officials have said.

item.title: WATCH: Firefighters give kids a superhero surprise
item.description: Corpus Christi firefighters dressed as superheroes surprised patients at Driscoll Children's Hospital by rappelling down the glass building as kids waved.

item.title: Democrats flip statehouses in midterm wave
item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's grandparents reflect on his historic Senate win
item.description: Judy and Jan Johnson spoke with ABC News Live about how proud they are to see their grandson, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, be elected to Senate.

item.title: Secret Service finds man parked near White House with multiple firearms: Authorities
item.description: The suspect, Ronny Guanipa-Chrinos, allegedly made threats to kill President Donald Trump, according to DHS.

item.title: Latino vote helped thwart Texas Republicans' redistricting effort
item.description: Last year, the Republican-controlled Texas legislature redrew its congressional maps aimed at giving the GOP five more seats.

item.title: WATCH: Guide dog Eddie named 2026 American Humane Society Hero Dog
item.description: Eddie, a 3-year-old Labrador retriever, was honored for changing the life of his legally blind owner, Luis Rodriguez, through his work as a guide dog.

item.title: US attorney tasked with leading probe into Trump's foes resigns from DOJ
item.description: Jason Reding Quinones, the U.S. attorney tasked with leading a sweeping and controversial conspiracy probe targeting President Trump’s foes, has resigned from the DOJ.

item.title: WATCH: $11.4M shipment of Nvidia cargo stolen from Oakland
item.description: Experts describe the computer hardware theft as a sophisticated cargo heist.

item.title: WATCH: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s grandparents react to historic win in Michigan
item.description: Jan and Judy Johnson, grandparents of Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, join ABC News Live to reflect on his Senate victory, their blended interfaith family and the traditions that bring them together.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Fall’s beautiful colors on display at Utah’s Zion National Park
item.description: You can see more about Zion and other national parks on "National Parks USA," streaming now on Disney+.

item.title: WATCH: 1st look at Nat Geo's 'Wolves Up Close with Bertie Gregory'
item.description: The new National Geographic documentary follows Bertie Gregory to Canada's Hudson Bay as he captures rare wolf behaviors during the harsh Arctic winter.

item.title: WATCH: Multiple water rescues amid flood emergencies in the South
item.description: A flood emergency is underway across multiple states in the South – triggering dozens of water rescues in Florida, Georgia and Tennessee in the middle of the night.

item.title: WATCH: These identical twin sisters speak at the same time
item.description: Danny New talks to identical twin sisters in Australia who are turning heads for their unique speech patterns.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities reveal motive in Citibank complex shooting
item.description: Chilling surveillance video shows a gunman exchanging gunfire with a security guard after ramming a gate at a Citibank complex near Tampa and killing a woman having lunch, authorities say.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the man who's the new voice of Boston's Logan airport
item.description: Christopher Donisi, an HVAC pipe fitter, will be the man behind the first voice travelers hear when they land in Beantown in the near future.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.title: WATCH: Bob Dylan, Prince William, Prince Harry: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC News' Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including Bob Dylan meeting with Pope Leo at the Vatican and Prince William and Prince Harry joining forces to honor their mother.
